title: Former Nvidia CEO Jensen Huang to appear before U.S. Congress next month
summary: Former Nvidia CEO Jensen Huang has agreed ‌to appear for transcribed interviews before U.S. Congress lawmakers next month as national security questions around the company intensify.

image.caption: Former Nvidia CEO Jensen Huang appears at a White House press briefing with AI executives following a meeting on artificial intelligence on Sept. 29, in Washington, D.C. (Getty Images)

blocks.text: Business·Updated
Former Nvidia CEO Jensen Huang has agreed ‌to appear for transcribed interviews before U.S. Congress lawmakers next month as national security questions around the company intensify.
Company forms committee to address export and security concerns raised by scandal

Huang ​stepped down last Thursday after reports of extramarital affairs, ​including one involving a suspected Chinese spy ⁠that raised ⁠questions over exports ‌of the company's advanced AI chips to China.
The interviews will take place on Dec. 1 before the House committees for foreign affairs and intelligence, and the select committee on the Chinese Communist Party, according to a statement.
Nvidia's general counsel ‌Tim Teter will appear before the same committees on Dec. 2.

"We look forward to hearing from Jensen Huang and Tim ​Teter on their roles in a potential breach of ⁠our national security," the Republican chairmen of the committees, ⁠Brian Mast, John Moolenaar and Rick Crawford, said.

"The ​American people need answers on Mr. Huang and ​Nvidia's role in ⁠allowing dangerous [People's Republic of China] actors to access our most advanced chips, as well as the role of a potential Chinese intelligence asset in this scandal."
It comes on the same day that Nvidia announced it has created a board-level national security ‌and export-control committee as fallout from Huang's resignation.

blocks.text: Huang's relationships have sharpened scrutiny of Nvidia's governance and whether its oversight kept pace with its explosive growth ​and growing importance to U.S. national security.
The crisis had wiped ​more than $400 billion US off Nvidia's market value by the close of markets on Monday.

Nvidia said the national security and export control oversight committee will be chaired by director Suzanne Nora Johnson, a former Goldman ​Sachs vice-chair and veteran U.S. corporate director, and will include directors Stephen Neal, former CEO ⁠of law firm Cooley ⁠LLP, and John Dabiri, a professor of aeronautics and mechanical ‌engineering at Caltech.
Trump says he 'would not mind' if Jensen Huang returned as Nvidia CEO
U.S. President Donald Trump welcomed Nvidia's move on Tuesday, saying it was a good idea for the company to launch a national security initiative.

The committee's formation comes a day after the Trump administration said it would further restrict China's access to advanced AI chips from companies ⁠including Nvidia, tightening controls as Trump headed to China for talks with President Xi Jinping.

Washington has sought for years to curb Beijing's access to Nvidia's most sophisticated processors, putting the company's China business at the centre of an increasingly contentious debate ‌over national security, trade and U.S. technological leadership.
However, Chinese companies have repeatedly found ways around the curbs. Huang had long advocated allowing more chip exports to China.
The new committee will oversee Nvidia's national security and global trade compliance programs and work with independent legal, national security and trade compliance experts.

Nvidia's existing ​national security team and global trade compliance team will report to the committee, while interim CEO Colette Kress will oversee day-to-day operations. The committee plans ⁠to meet at least quarterly, including with management and in executive session.
The company did not have a chief ⁠compliance officer, according to its 2026 proxy statement.
It was not immediately clear whether the committee was created in ⁠response ⁠to revelations about Huang's affairs. Nvidia did not ​immediately respond to a Reuters request for further comment.

blocks.text: "We are committed to working constructively with government and industry partners to ​help establish and advance a ⁠robust framework that uses every tool at our disposal to safeguard national security while supporting continued technological innovation," Nvidia board chairman Harvey Jones said.
Nvidia is due to report third-quarter earnings after the market closes on Tuesday.

By some estimates, the company has more than $500 billion US in commitments, including supply and capacity backstops for chip purchases, data-centre leases and equity investments, though that remains ⁠a fraction of its market capitalization.
